summary.text: Solid sodium metal reacts with chlorine gas to make a new solid called sodium chloride.
summary.excerpt: Solid sodium metal reacts with chlorine gas to produce solid sodium chloride.

summary.text: This is a combination reaction, where two elements join together to form a compound, a substance made of both.
summary.excerpt: One combination reaction is two elements combining to form a compound.

bondingType.text: Sodium chloride, also called table salt, is an ionic compound.
bondingType.excerpt: Sodium chloride, also known as salt, common salt, table salt or halite, is an ionic compound

bondingWhy.text: A sodium atom passes an electron over to a chlorine atom.
bondingWhy.excerpt: An electron transfers from the Na atom to the Cl atom

bondingWhy.text: Particles with opposite electric charges, called ions, pull on each other, and this pull is called an ionic bond.
bondingWhy.excerpt: The attraction between oppositely charged ions is called an ionic bond

hazard.text: Sodium catches fire very easily, and touching water, acids or halogens can make it burn or explode.

hazard.text: Chlorine is a greenish yellow gas that is poisonous to breathe in.
